proposals.before: When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang, and others rose up, dozens of generals who were seizing territory passed through Gaoyang. Li Sheng heard that their generals all grasped the reins tightly, favored harsh rituals, acted arbitrarily, and could not listen to broad-minded words. Li Sheng then deeply hid himself away.
proposals.after: When Chen Sheng, Xiang Liang, and others rose up, dozens of generals who were seizing territory passed through Gaoyang. Li Sheng heard that their generals were all petty and cramped, fond of harsh etiquette, self-willed, and unable to listen to broad-minded words. Li Sheng then hid himself away deeply.
proposals.reason: 握齱 means petty and cramped, not grasping reins; 苛禮 is punctilious harsh etiquette.

proposals.before: When the cavalryman returned, Li Sheng met him and said: "I have heard that Pei Gong is arrogant but treats people easily, with many great strategies. This is truly someone I wish to follow and travel with. Do not speak for me first.
proposals.after: When the cavalryman returned, Li Sheng met him and said: "I have heard that Pei Gong is arrogant but easy with people, and has many great strategies. This is truly someone I wish to follow. There is no one to introduce me first.
proposals.reason: 莫為我先 means no one will introduce him first, not an instruction not to speak for him first.

proposals.before: Cavalry gentleman returned. Li Sheng met and told him: "I have heard Pei Gong is arrogant but treats people easily, has many great strategies. This truly is what I wish to follow and travel with. Do not speak for me first.
proposals.after: The cavalryman returned. Li Sheng met him and told him: "I have heard Pei Gong is arrogant but easy with people, and has many great strategies. This truly is what I wish to follow and travel with. There is no one to introduce me first.
proposals.reason: 騎士 is a cavalryman, not a gentleman; 莫為我先 is lack of an introducer, not a prohibition on speaking first.

proposals.before: Cavalry gentleman said: 'Pei Gong not fond of Confucians, various guests wearing Confucian caps coming ones, Pei Gong promptly loosens their caps, urinates wet among them.
proposals.after: The cavalryman said: 'Pei Gong is not fond of Confucians. Whenever guests come wearing Confucian caps, Pei Gong promptly loosens their caps and urinates into them.
proposals.reason: 騎士 is cavalryman; 溲溺其中 means he urinates into the caps, not urinates wet among them.

proposals.before: Li Sheng arrived and entered to announce himself. Pei Gong was just sitting cross-legged on the bed having two women wash his feet, and he saw Li Sheng.
proposals.after: Li Sheng arrived and entered to announce himself. Pei Gong was just sitting arrogantly on the bed having two women wash his feet, and he received Li Sheng.
proposals.reason: 倨床 is an arrogant lounging posture, not specifically sitting cross-legged; 見 here is receiving the visitor.

proposals.before: Huaiyin was just attacking Qi to the east. King Han was repeatedly in distress at Xingyang and Chenggao, and planned to abandon Chenggao and the territory to its east, garrisoning Gong and Luo to resist Chu.
proposals.after: Huaiyin was just attacking Qi to the east. The King of Han was repeatedly in distress at Xingyang and Chenggao, and planned to abandon Chenggao and the territory to its east, garrisoning Gong and Luo to resist Chu.
proposals.reason: Literal English renders 漢王 as 'King Han', which reads as a personal name rather than the title King of Han.

proposals.before: I wish your excellency to urgently advance troops again, take Xingyang, occupy Aocang's grain, block Chenggao's defiles, cut off the road through Daxing, hold the mouth of Feihu at a distance, and guard Baima's ford. Show the feudal lords the force of real control, and then the whole realm will know where to turn.
proposals.after: I wish your excellency to urgently advance troops again, take Xingyang, occupy Aocang's grain, block Chenggao's defiles, cut off the road through Taihang, hold the mouth of Feihu, and guard Baima's ford. Show the feudal lords the force of real control, and then the whole realm will know where to turn.
proposals.reason: 大行 is the Taihang range (as in s0070 大行之阪), not a place named Daxing; 距 here means hold/resist the pass, not 'at a distance'.

proposals.before: The King of Han was the first to enter Xianyang, but the King of Xiang broke the covenant and instead of granting him the kingship, banished him to Hanzhong.
proposals.after: The King of Han was the first to enter Xianyang, but the King of Xiang broke the covenant and, instead of granting him that kingship, made him king of Hanzhong.
proposals.reason: 王之漢中 means Xiang Yu made him king in Hanzhong, not that he was banished there; the literal already has enfeoffing.

proposals.before: he defeated Northern Wei and captured thirty-two cities. This was the army of Chiyou, not achieved through human effort but through heaven's blessing.
proposals.after: he defeated the Wei of the north and captured thirty-two cities. This was the army of Chiyou, not achieved through human effort but through heaven's blessing.
proposals.reason: 北魏 here is the northern Wei polity of the Chu-Han war, not the later Northern Wei dynasty.

proposals.before: When the Marquis of Huaiyin heard that Li Yiji had, merely by leaning on the crossbar of his carriage and speaking, won over more than seventy cities of Qi, he crossed his forces over the plain by night and launched a surprise attack on Qi.
proposals.after: When the Marquis of Huaiyin heard that Li Yiji had, merely by leaning on the crossbar of his carriage and speaking, won over more than seventy cities of Qi, he crossed his forces at Pingyuan by night and launched a surprise attack on Qi.
proposals.reason: 平原 here is the place Pingyuan, not a generic plain; Han Xin crossed the Yellow River at Pingyuan to attack Qi.

proposals.before: When the Marquis of Huaiyin heard that Li Sheng had bowed in his carriage and brought Qi seventy-odd cities to submission, he crossed his troops through the plain by night and attacked Qi.
proposals.after: When the Marquis of Huaiyin heard that Li Sheng had leaned on his carriage crossbar and brought Qi seventy-odd cities to submission, he crossed his troops at Pingyuan by night and attacked Qi.
proposals.reason: 伏軾 is leaning on the carriage crossbar, not bowing; 平原 is Pingyuan.

proposals.before: In the time of Gaozu, when the Central Kingdoms had just been pacified, Zhao Tuo had subdued Nanyue and was made its king.
proposals.after: In the time of Gaozu, when the Central Kingdoms had just been pacified, Zhao Tuo had subdued Nanyue and thereupon made himself its king.
proposals.reason: 因王之 means Zhao Tuo made himself king of Nanyue, not that he was passively made king.

proposals.before: When Gaozu was emperor and the central states had just been pacified, Wei Tuo pacified Nanyue, so Gaozu enfeoffed him as king.
proposals.after: When Gaozu was emperor and the central states had just been pacified, Wei Tuo pacified Nanyue and thereupon made himself king.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has no subject Gaozu for 因王之; the literal invents an enfeoffment by Gaozu.

proposals.before: When Lu Jia arrived, Wei Tuo received him barefoot with his hair tied up, sitting cross-legged on a winnowing basket.
proposals.after: When Lu Jia arrived, Wei Tuo received him with hair in a mallet-shaped knot, sitting sprawled with legs splayed.
proposals.reason: 魋結 is a barbarian mallet-knot hairstyle and 箕倨 is an insolent splayed-leg sit; the text does not say barefoot or a winnowing basket as furniture.

proposals.before: Lu Jia replied: 'Your Majesty resembles worthiness.'
proposals.after: Lu Jia replied: 'Your Majesty seems the worthier.'
proposals.reason: 王似賢 answers the comparison and means Zhao Tuo appears somewhat the more worthy, not that he merely resembles worthiness.

proposals.before: Wei Tuo laughed heartily and said: 'If I had not arisen in the central states, how could I have become king here?
proposals.after: Wei Tuo laughed heartily and said: 'I did not arise in the central states, and so I am king here.
proposals.reason: 吾不起中國，故王此 is a statement of fact (he did not rise in the central states, therefore he rules Nanyue), not a counterfactual about becoming king.

proposals.before: The Gao Emperor cursed him and said: 'Your Lordship obtained the empire on horseback—what need have you for the Poetry and Documents!'
proposals.after: The Gao Emperor cursed him and said: 'I, your old man, obtained the empire on horseback—what need have I for the Poetry and Documents!'
proposals.reason: 乃公 is Gaozu’s self-reference (‘I, your old man’), not an address calling Lu Jia ‘Your Lordship’; 安事詩書 is the speaker’s own rhetorical question.

proposals.before: Chen Ping said: 'What can be done about it?'
proposals.after: 'What can be done about it?'
proposals.reason: The Chinese unit is only the quoted continuation 為之柰何; the literal line invents a second ‘Chen Ping said’ already supplied by s0139.

proposals.before: Chen Ping then bestowed upon Lu Jia a hundred slave women, fifty teams of carriages and horses, and five million cash for his food and drink expenses.
proposals.after: Chen Ping then bestowed upon Lu Jia a hundred male and female slaves, fifty teams of carriages and horses, and five million cash for his food and drink expenses.
proposals.reason: 奴婢 denotes male and female slaves, not slave women only.

proposals.before: When he was successfully released, he was deeply astonished.
proposals.after: When Pingyuan Jun had succeeded in getting him released, he was then deeply astonished.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 及其成功出之 credits the successful extraction to the prior plot (Pingyuan Jun), not a vague passive release; the current English hides the agent of 成功.

proposals.before: During the Xiaowen Emperor's time, the King of Huainan killed the Marquis of Biyang because of his ties to the Lü clansmen.
proposals.after: During the Xiaowen Emperor's time, King Li of Huainan killed the Marquis of Biyang because of his ties to the Lü clansmen.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits the posthumous name 厲 in 淮南厲王, already rendered as King Li in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: As for the Lord of Pingyuan, the gentleman was on good terms with me, which is why I was able to discuss it fully.
proposals.after: As for the Lord of Pingyuan, his son was on good terms with me, which is why I was able to discuss it fully.
proposals.reason: The sequence 平原君子 is 平原君 plus 子 (son), not the compound 君子 (gentleman); the idiomatic English already renders the kinship correctly.

decisions.reason: 握齱 denotes petty, cramped character, not gripping reins; 苛禮 is punctilious harsh etiquette. The original mistranslates 握齱.

decisions.after: When the cavalryman returned, Li Sheng met him and said: "I have heard that Pei Gong is arrogant but treats people easily, with many great strategies. This is truly someone I wish to follow and travel with. There is no one to introduce me first."
decisions.reason: 莫為我先 means there is no introducer, not a command not to speak; the proposed line wrongly drops 從游, which is follow-and-associate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 此真吾所願從游，莫為我先

decisions.reason: 騎士 is a cavalryman, not a gentleman, and 莫為我先 is the lack of an introducer, not a prohibition on speaking first.
騎士 is cavalryman; 溲溺其中 means he urinates into the loosened caps, not that he urinates wet among the guests.
倨床 is an insolent reclining posture, not specifically sitting cross-legged, and 見酈生 is receiving him in audience, not merely seeing him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 沛公方倨床使兩女子洗足，而見酈生

decisions.reason: 漢王 is the title King of Han, not a personal name King Han.
大行 is the Taihang range, as later 大行之阪 confirms; 距蜚狐之口 means hold/resist the Feihu mouth, not hold it at a distance.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 杜大行之道，距蜚狐之口

decisions.reason: 王之漢中 means Xiang Yu made the King of Han king in Hanzhong, not that he banished him there after withholding kingship altogether.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 項王負約不與而王之漢中

decisions.reason: 北魏 here is Wei to the north in the Chu-Han war, not the later Northern Wei dynasty; the original capitalized name is misleading.
平原 is the place Pingyuan, the crossing used to strike Qi, not a generic plain.
伏軾 is leaning on the carriage crossbar, not bowing; 平原 is Pingyuan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 酈生伏軾下齊七十餘城，乃夜度兵平原襲齊

decisions.reason: 因王之 has Wei Tuo as subject: after pacifying Nanyue he made himself its king; the passive 'was made' invents an external grant in this sentence.
The clause 因王之 has no Gaozu subject; the original invents an enfeoffment by Gaozu that the Chinese does not state here.
魋結 is a mallet-shaped hair knot and 箕倨 is an insolent splayed sit; the original invents being barefoot and sitting on a winnowing basket.
王似賢 answers 孰與…賢 by hedging that the king seems the more worthy, not that he merely resembles the abstract quality of worthiness.
吾不起中國，故王此 is a factual causal statement, not a counterfactual; the following unit 使我居中國 supplies the contrary-to-fact.
乃公 is Gaozu’s crude self-reference, so he is the one who won the empire on horseback and asks what use he has for the Poetry and Documents; the original wrongly addresses Lu Jia as Your Lordship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃公居馬上而得之，安事詩書

decisions.reason: This unit is only the quoted continuation 為之柰何; 陳平曰 already belongs to the preceding unit, so repeating it invents a second speech tag.
奴婢 is male and female slaves, not slave women only.

decisions.after: When the Lord of Pingyuan had succeeded in getting him released, he was then deeply astonished.
decisions.reason: 成功出之 makes Pingyuan Jun the agent who got the marquis released; the original hides that agent, but the proposal’s ‘Pingyuan Jun’ breaks this chapter’s idiomatic naming ‘the Lord of Pingyuan’.
淮南厲王 includes the posthumous name 厲, which the original literal omits.
平原君子 is 平原君 plus 子 (his son), not 君子 ‘gentleman’; the original misparses the kinship.

claimRevisions.reason: The unit’s 北魏 is Wei to the north in the Chu-Han war; capitalized Northern Wei as an English place value copies the mistranslation as the later dynasty name.
